Written by Daniel Kuhn | Edited by Kyle Baird

Happy Thursday! Daniel here on the last day I'll be filling in for James. *Bitcoin* is pressing toward $65,000 ( https://www.theblock.co/post/410163/paid-to-wait-bitcoin-presses-toward-65000-as-treasuries-out-yield-carry-trade-for-only-second-time-on-record?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) amid softer U.S. economic data, while Glassnode notes that Treasurys are out-yielding the crypto carry trade for only the second time on record, leaving institutional buyers "paid to wait" in cash and driving spot volumes to their lowest levels since 2019.

Meanwhile, *Quantum Solutions* is no longer the top *ETH treasury* in Japan after its latest sale ( https://www.theblock.co/post/410175/quantum-solutions-loses-top-japan-eth-treasury-spot-1-9-million-sale?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ).

*⏳ Bipartisan Sens. Tillis and Gallego send new ethics compromise to White House in Clarity Act push*

CZ ( https://www.theblock.co/post/410193/bipartisan-sens-tillis-gallego-new-ethics-compromise-white-house-clarity-act-push?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

*Senators Thom Tillis* (R-N.C.) and *Ruben Gallego* (D-Ariz.) sent a fresh bipartisan ethics compromise related to the *Clarity Act* crypto market structure legislation to the *White House* on Thursday morning.

* Lawmakers face a tight deadline to advance the bill through the Senate before the chamber recesses on Aug. 7, and it currently lacks the *60 votes* needed for passage amid reservations from both parties.
* Democrats have pushed for stronger ethics provisions to address potential conflicts involving *President Trump’s* crypto interests, including his family ties to *World Liberty Financial*.

Hello from the FT newsroom, where we are closely following the sell-off of tech equities.  Investor concerns about AI overspending have rocked semiconductor stocks, hitting Asian markets particularly hard. South Korean chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics tumbled on Tuesday, while a rout in US chip and memory stocks temporarily dragged the Nasdaq 100 into correction territory. Anxieties about the levels of financing and regulation were intensified following proposals for the US administration to restrict Chinese AI models. In an interview with the FT, Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg said this would not be “an effective solution”, contrary to the stances of the bosses of Anthropic and OpenAI.  Meanwhile, the UK market has benefited from its low exposure to tech, with the FTSE 100 reaching a record high in early trading yesterday. Its skew towards energy and finance had proved a useful means of diversification, analysts said, with Barclays’ head of European equity strategy labelling it an “almost anti-tech index”.  My choices this week As firefighters in France and Spain struggle to contain wildfire outbreaks, Australia offers some useful lessons on proactive prevention. Early warning systems, firebreaks and lowering household risks can help “put the fires out five years before they start”. (Free to read) Kyiv is changing its tactics to force Russian refineries offline for longer to increase the costs of the war for Moscow, the FT’s Ukraine correspondent Christopher Miller explains. The levels of uranium contained in cobalt exported by the Democratic Republic of Congo between 2000 and 2024 were enough to create 600 nuclear weapons, new research suggests. An FT and Lighthouse Reports investigation sheds light on the murky practice. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has suggested he is open to raising taxes to fund extensive social care reform, adding that he is prepared to use his “political capital” to tackle the issue. On Tuesday, the FT revealed that Fifa plans to sell a stake in a new $20bn commercial entity. The proposal has been met with a backlash from Europe and North America’s football governing bodies.
